sentences.text: As per the case of prosecution, Aarti Goud reported to Police Station Civil Lines, District Morena on 06.09.2022 that she was married to Vipul Singh S/o of Shri Jagdish Prasad on 07.12.2021.
After 15 days of marriage, her father- in-law Jagdish, mother-in-law Sunita, husband Vipul, brother-in-law Vivek and sister-in-law Sakshi started harassing her with regard to demand of dowry.
The accused used to abuse her in filthy language and harassed her mentally and physically.
She informed her parents.
In March, 2022, before festival of Holi, her husband Vipul, father-in-law Jagdish and mother-in-law Sunita forcefully administered abortion pill.
Thereafter, she underwent an abortion.
She tried to report the matter, but the accused admitted their mistake and requested her not to report.
On 31.08.2022, the accused assaulted her.
She sustained injuries on her neck and head.
Her husband snatched and damaged her mobile phone.
She informed her parents through her company.
Her parents came to her matrimonial home on 01.09.2022.
She returned to her parental home.
After recovering from incident, she is reporting.

On such allegations, Police Station Civil Lines registered FIR at Crime No.806/2022 for offence punishable under Sections 498A, 313, 323, 294,
506, 34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against Jagdish, Sunita, Vipul, Vivek and Sakshi Goud.
Thereafter, complainant was forwarded to medico legal examination.
Statements of witnesses have been recorded.
Relevant seizures have been made.
Sakshi Goud and Vivek Goud were arrested.
Investigation is underway.

Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicants are falsely implicated in the matter for the reason that they are parents of Vipul,
husband of complainant.
Minor matrimonial discord between husband and wife is aggravated and reported, involving the applicants.

Learned counsel referring to the duty certificate of applicant,
Jagdish Prasad submits that Jagdish Prasad is working as Naib Tehsildar at Assam Rifles, Shillong.
He was on duty from 1.03.2022 to 13.03.2022 and from 24.08.2022 to 31.08.2022, therefore, he was not present during both the alleged incidents.
Learned counsel further referring to the photographs and receipts of darshan at Ujjain submits that on 14.03.2022, entire family had gone for darshan to Ujjain.
Therefore, both the allegations against the applicants are false and fabricated.

Learned counsel further submits that applicant Jagdish Prasad is Naib Tehsildar in Assam Rifles,
Shillong.
No criminal antecedent is reported against him and his wife Sunita.
Jail incarceration on such allegations would bring social disrepute and great hardship to the applicants.
Applicants are ready to cooperate in the investigation.
There is no likelihood of their absconsion leaving behind their family and property.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the investigation or evidence by the applicants.

Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail Per contra,
learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application for grant of anticipatory bail on the ground of gravity of offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary and documents.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicants.
Thus, the application is allowed.
